title: Real-time electronic feedback and directly observed hand hygiene compliance on hospital wards: a paired cluster randomised trial
abstract: Objective: to test whether real-time badge feedback with weekly ward dashboards increases directly observed hand hygiene compliance compared with silent monitoring. Design: cluster randomised trial of 16 adult wards randomised in eight pairs sharing float staff, January to June 2027. Primary outcome: compliance at patient-zone entry observed by external observers equally visible on both arms. Results and conclusions will be written after the trial.
introduction: Electronic monitoring vendors report large gains in compliance, but most evaluations measure the outcome with the feedback system itself. The only retrieved randomised trial has since corrected its main result.
methods: Pairs of wards sharing float staff are allocated by a stratified sequence. External observers record opportunities in random sessions. The primary analysis is a mixed-effects logistic model adjusted for ward baseline compliance and specialty.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the flow of wards and observation sessions, observed and badge compliance by arm, and results for float staff separately.
discussion: The discussion will compare observed and badge-measured effects, consider observer visibility and contamination, and state what the result means for the licence.
limitations: Observer visibility; 16 wards; infections not evaluable; the planning effect size rests on a corrected record.
conclusion: To be written after the trial; it will be limited to observed compliance and will not claim effects on infection.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for cluster randomised trials
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty until the trial ends.
